lines.text: What Do We Eat in a Week?
Aarav's question is a good one, and the honest answer is that we
cannot say much about food in general until we look at food in
particular. So begin with the food you know best: your own.
Most of us eat without paying attention. We eat what is served, at
the time it is served, and we rarely notice the pattern. But there is
a pattern. Over a week, your meals repeat, vary, and cluster in
ways that tell you something about your household, your region,
Scientists call this kind of careful watching observation.
Observation is not the same as looking. Looking is what you
do all day. Observing is looking with a question in mind, and
You will need: your notebook, seven days.
Copy Table 3.1 into your notebook, leaving four lines for each day.
